This paired tutorial is generated from the same sources as the website. Code blocks are shown without executing during vignette rendering; the shared documentation script verifies the examples directly. Inputs are synthetic unless explicitly marked as repository files. Run the setup once before the workflows.

## Shared setup {#shared-setup}


```{r example-1, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
seqs <- data.frame(accver = c("A", "B", "C"), length = c(1000, 800, 1200))
links <- data.frame(qaccver = c("A", "B"), saccver = c("B", "C"),
  qstart = c(100, 200), qend = c(350, 500),
  sstart = c(150, 400), send = c(400, 700), pident = c(96, 89))
genes <- data.frame(accver = c("A", "B", "C"),
  start = c(150, 200, 400), end = c(300, 350, 650),
  strand = c("+", "+", "-"), anno = c("target", "target", "target"))
```


## Install and start {#installation}

### Requirements {#installation-requirements}
Use R ≥ 4.1.0 and ggplot2 ≥ 4.0.0. ggchord itself needs no compiled code.
Optional interval adapters use Bioconductor packages; spreadsheet imports need
readxl. Install these only for the input formats you actually use.

### Choose a source {#installation-source}
The GitHub repository is the installation source. A development checkout can
contain changes newer than a formal release; record its commit for reproducibility.
A CRAN release is not claimed by this guide.

```{r example-2, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("DangJem/ggchord")
library(ggchord)
packageVersion("ggchord")
```

For the checked-out 0.16.5 source, run from the repository root:

```{r example-3, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("pkgload")
pkgload::load_all(".")
```

Repository paths used in the [file-import example](#data-import) are not
installed package data. The introductory examples instead construct small data
frames in R and work after installation.

### First steps {#installation-first-steps}
Read the [data contract](#data), copy the [shared setup](#shared-setup),
then choose [a coordinate system](#modes). Save with explicit width and height;
RStudio's Plots pane can rearrange labels when resized.


## Data and coordinates {#data}

### Tables {#data-tables}
| Input | Required fields | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sequence | `accver`, `length` | Unique ID; positive full length in bp |
| Interval link | `qaccver`, `saccver`, `qstart`, `qend`, `sstart`, `send` | Query and subject anchors |
| Gene | `accver`, `start`, `end`, `strand` | Known `+`/`-`; optional `anno` |
| Feature | `accver`, `start`, `end`, `strand` or declared direction | May retain unknown strand; optional `type`, `label`, `feature_id` |

Identifiers may be arbitrary strings. Accession versions are preserved exactly.
`pident` and alignment `length` are optional unless a mapping, filter or statistic
needs them. A feature interval does not imply a sequence's full length.

### Coordinate contract {#data-coordinates}
Genomic coordinates are **one-based, inclusive bp**. BED/PAF readers convert their
source conventions; do not convert twice. Gene endpoints are ordered with
strand stored separately; link endpoint order may encode direction. A one-bp
link without direction evidence stays unknown. Unknown strand is never silently
changed to `+`; use `geom_feature()` instead of the strict gene layer.

Amino-acid coordinates require [explicit CDS projection](#projection).
Native Cartesian layout units, genomic bp, angles in degrees, physical mm and
track value units are different domains. See the full
data contract (`help("ggchord_data_contract", package = "ggchord")`).

### Import original records {#data-import}
Run this repository-only example from its root. Original files are not rewritten.


```{r example-4, eval=FALSE}
seq_files <- read_fasta_lengths(files = "examples/fasta/*.fna", source_file = TRUE)
link_files <- read_blast(files = "examples/blastn/*.o7", source_file = TRUE)
feature_files <- read_gff3(files = "examples/gff3/*.gff3", unstranded = "keep", source_file = TRUE)
```


`read_genbank()` retains record/feature provenance and segmented locations.
`read_bed()` and `read_paf()` retain their conversion metadata. `as_ggchord_seq()`,
`as_ggchord_feature()` and `as_ggchord_link()` adapt supported S4 objects; provide
full lengths and IDs explicitly when the object lacks them. `file` and `files` both accept path vectors or globs; repeated resolved paths
are read once in first-occurrence order. Choose one clear entry for a workflow. Missing sequence or
homology data must be supplied by the analyst, not invented by the plotting layer.

### Validate, clean, prepare {#data-validation}
After the [shared setup](#shared-setup):


```{r example-5, eval=FALSE}
validation <- validate_ggchord_data(seqs, links, genes)
cleaned <- clean_ggchord_data(seqs, links, genes)
prepared <- prepare_ggchord_data(seqs, links, features = list(genes = genes))
```


Validation reports issues; cleaning makes explicit repairs with a report.
Preparation combines workflow steps without inferring biological membership.
Inspect `validation`, `cleaned$report` and `prepared$report` before plotting.
`source_row` in geometry refers to the resolved layer input, while `.source_line`
means a physical file line; GenBank has separate record/feature provenance.
Aggregates may have `source_rows` and `.length_estimated` flags. Preserve these
when filtering or merging links.

### Inspect a problematic input and its repair report {#data-repairs}

```{r example-6, eval=FALSE}
problem_links <- data.frame(qaccver = c("A", "absent"), saccver = "B",
  qstart = c(80, 20), qend = c(20, 40), sstart = 50, send = 120, pident = c(103, 90))
problem_report <- validate_ggchord_data(seqs, problem_links)
repaired <- clean_ggchord_data(seqs, problem_links, unknown_id = "drop",
  reversed_interval = "sort", invalid_pident = "clip")
# Deliberate teaching repairs, not a recommendation to clip scientific values silently.
```

| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| `input_rows` | 2 |
| `retained_rows` | 1 |

The demonstration intentionally includes an unknown ID, reversed interval and
identity outside 0–100. These explicit repairs are not a recommendation to clip
scientific observations silently. Inspect `problem_report` and `repaired$report`,
retain the original table, and choose policies appropriate to actual evidence.
A legitimate reverse alignment can keep endpoint order instead of being sorted.
`prepare_ggchord_data()` therefore retains its workflow-specific default policy;
standalone cleaning and preparation should not be assumed identical.

### Declare genome and contig keys {#data-hierarchy}

```{r example-7, eval=FALSE}
contigs <- transform(seqs, genome = c("sample1", "sample1", "sample2"))
genomes <- data.frame(genome = c("sample1", "sample2"))
hierarchy <- validate_ggchord_hierarchy(contigs, genomes, strict = TRUE)
```


`hierarchy$contigs` summarizes declared membership without concatenating contigs.
No membership is inferred from an accession prefix. Provide globally unique IDs
when separate samples reuse local contig names. Use [file formats and adapters](#formats)
for format/optional-object details, and the [real-record tutorial](#real-data)
to carry reports into a complete figure.


## File formats and explicit adapters {#formats}

### Start with canonical roles {#formats-adapters}
Run the [shared setup](#shared-setup). A renamed column is an explicit
role mapping, not a request to rewrite accession versions or infer full lengths.


```{r example-8, eval=FALSE}
sequence_input <- as_ggchord_seq(data.frame(chrom = "A", size = 1000),
  mapping = c(accver = "chrom", length = "size"))
feature_input <- as_ggchord_feature(data.frame(chrom = "A", left = 10,
  right = 100, strand = "+"), mapping = c(accver = "chrom", start = "left", end = "right"))
link_input <- as_ggchord_link(links)
```


Inspect the ordinary returned tables and `ggchord_conversion` attributes.
`as_ggchord_seq()` requires known full lengths; `as_ggchord_feature()` preserves
unknown strands; `as_ggchord_link()` preserves anchors and available metadata.
The same adapters are used by supported direct S4 inputs to layers.

### BED and PAF: convert once {#formats-zero-based}
These files are deliberately synthetic. They demonstrate format conversion,
not a measured alignment or annotation of a real sequence.


```{r example-9, eval=FALSE}
bed_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".bed")
writeLines("A\t0\t100\tdemo\t0\t-", bed_path)
bed_features <- read_bed(bed_path)
paf_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".paf")
writeLines("A\t1000\t0\t100\t-\tB\t800\t200\t300\t95\t100\t255", paf_path)
paf_links <- read_paf(paf_path)
unlink(c(bed_path, paf_path))
```


The BED interval `0,100)` becomes one-based inclusive `1..100`. PAF negative
relative strand yields decreasing subject endpoints; mapq 255 is unavailable,
retained separately from the converted missing value. PAF identity is derived
from producer-reported counts, not recomputed from bases. Keep import attributes
and source-line columns; do not subtract or add one again before drawing.

### GenBank: records, segments and provenance {#formats-genbank}

```{r example-10, eval=FALSE}
# Optional reader: the selected Python must already contain Biopython.
genbank_result <- NULL
if (nzchar(Sys.which("python3")) && identical(suppressWarnings(system2("python3",
  c("-c", shQuote("from Bio import SeqIO")), stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE)), 0L)) {
  gb_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".gb")
  writeLines(c("LOCUS       demo                      12 bp    DNA     linear   BCT 01-JAN-2000",
    "DEFINITION  Synthetic teaching record.", "ACCESSION   demo", "VERSION     demo.1",
    "FEATURES             Location/Qualifiers", "     misc_feature    2..8",
    "                     /note=\"site\"", "ORIGIN", "        1 acgtacgtacgt", "//"), gb_path)
  genbank_result <- read_genbank(gb_path)
  unlink(gb_path)
}
```


This optional example runs only if the selected Python already has Biopython.
The function installs nothing. Its result contains `seq_data`, named
`features$annotation` and `report`; joined locations retain real segments and
source record/feature indices. Unknown lengths are not inferred from feature
ends. Use `unsupported = "report"` to retain unsupported locations in a report,
not to flatten them into guessed local intervals.

### Optional interval objects {#formats-ranges}

```{r example-11, eval=FALSE}
range_inputs <- NULL
if (requireNamespace("GenomicRanges", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ranges <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(seqnames = "A", ranges = IRanges::IRanges(10, 100),
    strand = "*", seqlengths = c(A = 1000L))
  range_inputs <- list(seq_data = as_ggchord_seq(ranges), features = as_ggchord_feature(ranges))
}
```

| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| `genbank` | SKIP: Biopython unavailable |
| `ranges` | SKIP: GenomicRanges unavailable |

The unknown strand `*` remains unknown. Known seqlengths come from Seqinfo,
not the largest observed interval. InteractionSet `GInteractions` additionally
adapts to links; keep a common region/length context and explicit biological
membership. Missing optional packages are reported as skipped in the example
record, not as validated support. See the complete [data contract (`help("ggchord_data_contract", package = "ggchord")`).


## Three coordinate systems {#modes}

Run the [shared setup](#shared-setup) once. Each object below is a normal
composable ggplot; print it or use `ggsave()`.

### Chord: compare multiple sequences {#modes-chord}

```{r example-12, eval=FALSE}
p_chord <- ggchord(seqs, links, genes) +
  geom_seq() + geom_link_ribbon() + geom_gene() + geom_seq_label() +
  coord_chord()
```

![Chord comparison of three synthetic sequences](../man/figures/chord.png)
`coord_chord()` controls global rotation and fitting. Sequence-local radius,
curvature, gap and orientation belong to `geom_seq()`. A NULL link control point
uses the historical origin-based chord route; it does not mean a universal
straight link. Ribbon avoidance defaults to `uniform`, line avoidance to `none`.

### Circular: annotate one sequence {#modes-circular}

```{r example-13, eval=FALSE}
features <- data.frame(accver = "A", start = c(80, 380, 700),
  end = c(280, 610, 850), strand = c("+", "-", "."),
  type = c("CDS", "CDS", "region"), label = c("alpha", "beta", "origin"))
p_circular <- ggchord(seqs[1, ]) + geom_seq() +
  geom_feature(data = features) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(data = features) + coord_circular() +
  theme_ggchord(axis = element_blank())
```

![Circular annotation with known and unknown strands](../man/figures/circular.png)
This example explicitly hides the axis to leave the feature labels clear.
`coord_circular()` requires a single sequence. General features can carry unknown
strand. `geom_feature_plasmid()` is a convenience preset with its own defaults;
choose it explicitly when those defaults fit the task. Primer and restriction
layers are described in [recognition](#recognition).

### Collinear: align local comparisons {#modes-collinear}

```{r example-14, eval=FALSE}
p_collinear <- ggchord(seqs, links, genes) +
  geom_link_ribbon(alpha = .3) + geom_seq() +
  geom_gene(position = position_strand(.1)) + geom_seq_label() +
  coord_collinear(anchor = genes[c("accver", "start", "end")],
    align = "center", orientation = "auto")
```

![Anchored linear sequence comparison](../man/figures/collinear.png)
`anchor` aligns specified intervals; `orientation = "auto"` chooses supported
orientations using available evidence. Inspect orientation diagnostics rather
than assuming biological inversion. Ribbons connect adjacent displayed rows by
default; use `adjacent_only = FALSE` or explicit `pairs` to retain others.
Non-adjacent outlines default to dashed; explicit styles take priority. These
rules differ from chord mode. [Focus and segments](#views) preserve source
coordinates for cropped or locally reversed views.


## From original records to sequence comparisons {#real-data}

This complete workflow uses four sequence records already present in the source
repository. It requires the matching development checkout or the tutorial input
bundle, not new alignments or external gene prediction. [Download the inputs](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples)
and unpack them so `examples/` is under the working directory. Record the package
version and [build manifest](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/website) with the exported figure.

### Read and inspect original records {#real-data-read}

```{r example-15, eval=FALSE}
seq_real <- read_fasta_lengths(files = "examples/fasta/*.fna", source_file = TRUE)
feature_real <- read_gff3(files = "examples/gff3/*.gff3", unstranded = "keep", source_file = TRUE)
link_real <- read_blast(files = "examples/blastn/*.o7", source_file = TRUE)
real_validation <- validate_ggchord_data(seq_real, link_real)
```


The FASTA headers supply exact accession versions and lengths. GFF3 contributes
CDS intervals and their original strands. BLAST output contributes existing
alignments; the reader does not run BLAST. Inspect `real_validation` before
continuing: decreasing link endpoints can be legitimate reverse-direction hits.
Never turn unknown annotation strands into `+` to make a gene shortcut accept them.

### Make the display selection explicit {#real-data-selection}

```{r example-16, eval=FALSE}
real_prepared <- prepare_ggchord_data(seq_real, link_real,
  features = list(annotation = feature_real))
real_filtered <- filter_ggchord_ribbons(link_real, min_pident = 80, min_length = 500)
# Explicit display subset: the six longest CDS per sequence; raw annotations stay intact.
display_rows <- unlist(lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(feature_real)), feature_real$accver),
  function(i) head(i[order(-(feature_real$end[i] - feature_real$start[i] + 1))], 6)))
real_display_features <- feature_real[display_rows, , drop = FALSE]
label_rows <- unlist(lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(real_display_features)), real_display_features$accver),
  function(i) head(i, 2)))
real_labels <- real_display_features[label_rows, , drop = FALSE]
```

| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| `sequences` | 4 |
| `features` | 266 |
| `displayed_chord_features` | 24 |
| `raw_links` | 32 |
| `displayed_links` | 8 |
| `labelled_features` | 8 |

The link display retains identity ≥80% and reported alignment length ≥500 bp.
The chord view selects the six longest imported CDS per sequence, labelling the
two longest of those. These are display rules, not biological findings or a claim
that omitted genes are absent. Raw `feature_real` and `link_real` remain intact;
`real_prepared$report` and `real_filtered$report` retain preparation/filter evidence.
No display strands are recoded. This differs from the small packaged teaching
fixture whose documented generation includes display-strand recoding.

### Build a chord comparison {#real-data-chord}

```{r example-17, eval=FALSE}
p_real_chord <- ggchord(seq_real, real_filtered$data, validate = "none") +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = pident), alpha = .35) + geom_seq() +
  geom_feature(aes(feature_fill = strand), data = real_display_features,
    width = .045, position = position_strand(.08)) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(data = real_labels, label_layout = "radial",
    label_wrap = 20, size = 2.5, position = position_strand(.08)) +
  geom_seq_label() + coord_chord() + theme_ggchord_publication() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

![Original sequence comparison with an explicit CDS display subset](../man/figures/realchord.png)

Read sequence labels first, then source-strand feature arrows and interval links.
Ribbons encode existing aligned intervals and mapped identity; their crossing is
not itself evidence of a rearrangement. The selected features remain visibly
separate from the much wider alignment spans. Use the full input tables when
scientific interpretation needs annotations outside this display subset.

### Inspect all annotations in a linear view {#real-data-linear}

```{r example-18, eval=FALSE}
p_real_linear <- ggchord(seq_real, real_filtered$data, validate = "none") +
  geom_link_ribbon(alpha = .25) + geom_seq() + geom_seq_label() +
  geom_feature(data = feature_real, position = position_strand(.08)) +
  geom_seq_scale(length = 10000) + coord_collinear() +
  theme_ggchord_publication() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

![Original sequences, all imported CDS and filtered alignment links](../man/figures/reallinear.png)

This view draws all imported annotations. Ribbons connect adjacent displayed
sequences by default; retaining every comparison is an explicit layer decision.
The bp scale bar belongs to collinear coordinates. See [local views](#views)
for cropping, source-coordinate axes and independent windows, and
[output](#output) to preview and save at the gallery's stated dimensions.

### Keep the evidence with the figure {#real-data-provenance}
The input archive contains unmodified FASTA/GFF3/BLAST files, a SHA256 manifest
and the shared example script. The plot manifest records the code hash, PNG device,
width, height and dpi. The accession names identify source records; a drawing is
not a replacement for the original annotations or alignment evidence.


## A complete circular annotation workflow {#plasmids}

### Use a source-backed sequence {#plasmids-input}
The bundled `plasmid_example_pUC19` is copied from the repository's original
`examples/plasmid/pUC19.fna`; bases and sequence identity are not edited for display.
The workflow uses the package's source-backed recognition catalogues. It needs no
network request or experimental measurements fabricated for the figure.


```{r example-19, eval=FALSE}
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
plasmid_features <- find_common_features(plasmid_example_pUC19)
plasmid_primers <- find_primer_bindings(plasmid_example_pUC19, set = "universal")
plasmid_sites <- find_restriction_sites(plasmid_example_pUC19)
display_sites <- filter_restriction_sites(plasmid_sites,
  enzymes = c("EcoRI", "BamHI", "HindIII"))
primer_names <- primer_catalog(set = "universal")
plasmid_position <- position_feature_stack(spacing = .085,
  base_position = position_plasmid())
p_plasmid <- ggchord(plasmid_example_pUC19) + geom_seq(seq_style = "double") +
  geom_feature_plasmid(data = plasmid_features, position = plasmid_position) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(data = plasmid_features, position = plasmid_position,
    label_fit = "shrink", label_min_size = 1.8) +
  geom_primer(data = plasmid_primers) +
  geom_primer_label_repel(data = plasmid_primers, max_overlaps = 0) +
  geom_restriction_site(data = display_sites) + geom_seq_center_label() +
  coord_circular(rotation = 90) + theme_ggchord_plasmid()
```

![pUC19 with source-backed features, primers and restriction sites](../man/figures/plasmid.png)
| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| `sequence_length` | 2686 |
| `features` | 9 |
| `primers` | 6 |
| `all_sites` | 49845 |
| `display_sites` | 3 |

### Read the annotation layers {#plasmids-layers}
The double backbone establishes one circular sequence. General features use a
plasmid preset and explicit stacking Position; labels use the same Position.
Primer arcs indicate binding ranges, restriction ticks indicate cleavage/display
positions, and the centre label identifies the sequence and length. A cropped or
filtered display does not change the full-sequence restriction count.

### Choose the displayed sites deliberately {#plasmids-sites}
`find_restriction_sites()` returns all matches. This figure explicitly selects
EcoRI, BamHI and HindIII so that a compact restriction cluster remains readable;
`plasmid_sites` retains the complete search result. The `reference` filter uses a saved
reference display set only when the complete supplied sequence matches that
reference. Other tasks can select `unique`, `six_plus` or explicit enzyme names.
Inspect `display_sites` and the site's methylation/source columns before drawing.
The reference set is a presentation choice, not a claim about an unknown sample.

### Understand catalogue and label limits {#plasmids-limits}
`primer_names` exposes catalogue entries. This example searches the universal catalogue exactly; reference primer
annotations and exact oligonucleotide searches have distinct provenance. Near-exact protein feature
recognition has the limitations in [recognition](#recognition); it does not
validate biological function or a primer experiment. Text can move, shrink within
its explicit minimum, or hide. Keep the geometry and inspect exported label
reasons at the final size rather than assuming every annotation must have text.

### Adapt the workflow {#plasmids-adapt}
For your own named DNA sequence, replace the input and inspect search results
before adding geoms. For externally curated annotations, pass your feature table
instead of running recognition. Use [stacking and shapes](#annotations) for
geometry, [labels](#labels) for fitting, and [output](#output) for devices.


## Prepare and summarize alignment links {#ribbons}

### Begin with the original link table {#ribbons-input}
Use the [real-record workflow](#real-data-selection) to create `seq_real`,
`link_real` and `real_filtered`. Keep its original tables and filter report.


```{r example-20, eval=FALSE}
unique_links <- deduplicate_ggchord_ribbons(real_filtered$data, by = "overlap",
  min_reciprocal_overlap = .9)
merged_links <- merge_ggchord_ribbons(unique_links$data, max_gap = 100,
  min_pident_difference = 2)
bundled_links <- bundle_ggchord_ribbons(link_real, seq_real, bins = 30)
p_density <- ggchord(seq_real, link_real, validate = "none") + geom_seq() +
  stat_ribbon_density(aes(ribbon_alpha = after_stat(density))) + coord_chord()
p_bundle <- ggchord(seq_real, link_real, validate = "none") + geom_seq() +
  stat_ribbon_bundle(bins = 30) + coord_chord()
```

| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| `filtered` | 8 |
| `deduplicated` | 8 |
| `merged` | 8 |
| `bundled` | 28 |

### Understand each transformation {#ribbons-transformations}
Filtering keeps observations meeting declared thresholds. Reciprocal-overlap
deduplication selects a representative existing observation; it does not sum
identities. Merging combines nearby compatible intervals into a display envelope.
Bundling groups nearby query/subject locations into an aggregate. Inspect each
`$report` and source-row membership, especially when extra metadata conflict.
The merged or bundled envelope is not a newly computed nucleotide alignment.
Estimated lengths retain their flags; unobserved identity is never invented.

### Density is an explicit statistic {#ribbons-density}
![Explicit density summary of original alignment links](../man/figures/density.png)

`stat_ribbon_density()` maps a computed density, and `stat_ribbon_bundle()` performs
its explicit aggregation during build. The ordinary ribbon geom still draws one
ribbon per row. Interpret count, reported length and identity weighting in their
own units; more opaque ribbons need not mean stronger independently validated
homology. A point anchor without direction evidence cannot acquire an aggregate
orientation merely because its endpoints are equal.

### Choose interval ribbons or point links {#ribbons-points}
After the [shared setup](#shared-setup):


```{r example-21, eval=FALSE}
points <- data.frame(qaccver = c("A", "A"), saccver = c("B", "C"),
  qpos = c(200, 200), spos = c(400, 600), support = c(4, 10))
p_points <- ggchord(seqs) + geom_seq() + geom_seq_label() +
  geom_link_line(aes(link_colour = support, link_linewidth = support), data = points,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(2, "mm"))) +
  scale_link_colour_gradientn(colours = c("#BBCFC8", "#265E55"), guide = guide_ggchord_colourbar(available_aes = "link_colour")) +
  scale_link_linewidth_continuous(range = c(.3, 1)) + coord_chord()
```

![Point-to-point links with declared synthetic support values](../man/figures/pointlinks.png)

Here `support` is a declared synthetic demonstration value. Lines use `qpos/spos`,
not interval ends, and an arrow points from query to subject. The line default
avoidance is `none`; ribbon avoidance is `uniform`. Global chord rotation belongs
to the coordinate system. Pair selection and adjacent-row defaults in linear
plots are covered in [three modes](#modes-collinear).

The point-link colour scale supplies `available_aes = "link_colour"` to its
colourbar explicitly. Ordinary ggplot2 colourbars and the wrapper default do not
accept every extended role; choose the matching role when making a custom guide.


## Features, stacking and genomic decoration {#annotations}

### Preserve feature semantics {#annotations-stack}
Run the [shared setup](#shared-setup). This synthetic table contains
overlapping CDS/regions and an unknown strand. Geometry and fill map separately
from the same category; an explicit fixed `shape` would override shape mapping.


```{r example-22, eval=FALSE}
stack_features <- data.frame(feature_id = paste0("f", 1:4), accver = "A",
  start = c(100, 150, 300, 650), end = c(350, 450, 550, 800),
  strand = c("+", "+", "-", "."), type = c("CDS", "region", "CDS", "region"),
  label = c("coding alpha", "overlap", "coding beta", "unstranded"))
stack_position <- position_feature_stack(spacing = .12)
p_stack <- ggchord(seqs[1, ]) + geom_seq() +
  geom_feature(aes(feature_fill = type, feature_shape = type), data = stack_features,
    position = stack_position) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(data = stack_features, position = stack_position) +
  scale_feature_shape_manual(values = c(CDS = "arrow", region = "block")) +
  scale_feature_fill_manual(values = c(CDS = "#4C8C7C", region = "#D3A05A")) + coord_collinear()
```

![Stacked synthetic features with mapped shapes and fills](../man/figures/featurestack.png)

`position_feature_stack()` resolves overlapping annotation lanes. The label layer
uses the same Position, so text anchors follow those lanes. Prefer unique
`feature_id` values for subset/reordered label inputs. The strict gene shortcut
requires known `+/-`; general features retain unknown/bidirectional semantics.

### Choose shapes by meaning {#annotations-shapes}
| Geometry | Typical use | Important distinction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `arrow`, `compact_arrow` | Directional coding/feature interval | Known direction is evidence, not a display guess |
| `block`, `capped_line` | Region or unfilled interval | Shape choice does not infer biological function |
| `promoter_arrow`, `primer_arrow`, `primer_arc` | Declared promoter/primer-style annotation | Computational matching and drawing are separate |
| `marker`, `chevron`, `lollipop` | Custom interval/point-like emphasis | Keep real interval metadata; display shape is a mapping |

`geom_gene()` and `geom_feature_plasmid()` are useful presets, not aliases with
identical defaults. Use `position_strand()` for signed offsets and
`position_plasmid()` as a circular placement preset; the latter is not a fourth
coordinate mode.

### Highlight an interval without rewriting observations {#annotations-decoration}

```{r example-23, eval=FALSE}
regions <- data.frame(accver = "A", start = 80, end = 420, category = "selected")
p_decorated <- ggchord(seqs, links) +
  geom_seq_region(aes(region_fill = category), data = regions) +
  geom_link_ribbon(alpha = .25) + geom_seq() + geom_seq_label() +
  scale_region_fill_manual(values = c(selected = "#E1B566")) +
  geom_seq_scale(length = 200) + coord_collinear()
```

![Region highlights and an independent bp reference bar](../man/figures/decorations.png)

A region overlay uses its own table and `region_fill` scale. `geom_seq_label()`
names sequences, `geom_seq_center_label()` supplies name/length in a single circle,
and `geom_seq_break()` marks cropped/segmented ends. `geom_seq_scale()` is an
independent bp reference bar for collinear plots; it differs from
`scale_seq_position_continuous()`, which controls genomic axes on sequences.
An ordinary ggplot2 annotation should use [position mapping](#views-mapping)
instead of treating bp as Cartesian x/y.


## Labels and local placement {#labels}

### Select a layout {#labels-layout}
Gene labels offer `"auto"`, `"radial"` and `"arc"` layouts. General feature
labels additionally support the internal-first `"feature"` default and external
`"callout"` layout. Choose the documented values for the layer you use; they are
not interchangeable presets.

After the [shared setup](#shared-setup):


```{r example-24, eval=FALSE}
p_labels <- ggchord(seqs, gene_data = genes) + geom_seq() +
  geom_gene() + geom_gene_label_repel(label_layout = "auto", size = 3) +
  coord_collinear()
```

![Automatic labels on a linear gene comparison](../man/figures/labels.png)

### Fixed and automatic placement {#labels-fixed}
Use `geom_gene_label()` or `geom_feature_label()` for manual `label_rotation`,
radial/circumferential offsets and orientation controls. Automatic layers reject
these manual controls: choose `label_layout` or remove the manual argument.
Use `size`, `colour` and `family` for supported fixed text styles.

`label_fit`, `label_wrap`, `label_max_lines` and `label_min_size` control fitting
where supported. Shrinking is explicit and bounded. Unresolved labels may move
or hide; the feature geometry remains. Inspect `label_fit_diagnostics` and
`label_diagnostics` at the final export size.

### Match anchors across layers {#labels-anchors}
In collinear mode, an omitted feature-label Position inherits an unambiguous
matching feature layer. Unique `feature_id` permits reordering or subsets, but
accession, interval and strand must agree. Multiple matching layers need an
explicit Position or unambiguous IDs. Preview after selecting the final device
size; resizing the Plots pane changes the available space.

### Compare the three gene layouts {#labels-comparison}

```{r example-25, eval=FALSE}
label_plots <- lapply(c("auto", "radial", "arc"), function(layout)
  ggchord(seqs, gene_data = genes) + geom_seq() + geom_gene() +
    geom_gene_label_repel(label_layout = layout, size = 3) + coord_chord() +
    labs(title = layout))
names(label_plots) <- c("auto", "radial", "arc")
p_manual_labels <- ggchord(seqs, gene_data = genes) + geom_seq() + geom_gene() +
  geom_gene_label(label_rotation = 30) + coord_collinear()
```

![Gene labels using auto placement](../man/figures/labelauto.png)
![Gene labels using radial placement](../man/figures/labelradial.png)
![Gene labels following sequence tangents](../man/figures/labelarc.png)

Print `label_plots$auto`, `$radial` or `$arc` to inspect a candidate. The inputs and
requested font size are identical; only the layout choice changes. Auto uses
shared columns where applicable, radial follows local contours and arc follows
the sequence tangent. `p_manual_labels` shows the separate fixed-label route;
its explicit rotation does not belong in an automatic repel layer.
General feature labels have additional internal-first/callout choices; see the
[complete circular workflow](#plasmids) for dense mixed annotation and
[stacking](#annotations-stack) for inherited or explicit Position anchors.


## Quantitative tracks {#tracks}

### Declare position and numerical domain {#tracks-domain}
After the [shared setup](#shared-setup):


```{r example-26, eval=FALSE}
bins <- data.frame(accver = "A", start = seq(1, 951, 50),
  end = seq(50, 1000, 50), signal = sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 20)))
p_tracks <- ggchord(seqs[1, ]) + geom_seq() +
  geom_track_bar(aes(track_value = signal, track_fill = signal), data = bins,
    position = position_track("signal", width = unit(5, "mm"))) +
  scale_track_value_continuous("signal", limits = c(-1, 1), unit = "arbitrary units") +
  scale_track_fill_gradientn("signal", colours = c("#31537D", "#F3F4EE", "#D26B38")) +
  coord_circular()
```

![Synthetic signal in an explicit quantitative track](../man/figures/tracks.png)

The signal is a synthetic sine wave in arbitrary units, not measured coverage or
GC skew. ggchord renders supplied values; it does not compute sequence composition.
Replace it with your measured bins and declare their actual unit.

### Share an ID deliberately {#tracks-sharing}
`position_track("signal", ...)` chooses placement and physical width.
`scale_track_value_continuous("signal", ...)` defines the numerical domain;
it is not spatial placement. Layers sharing an ID train one joint domain,
including the bar baseline, and must declare consistent track settings.
Fill/colour scales are separately scoped to that ID. `geom_track_tile()` encodes
categories, `geom_track_line()` connects numeric observations, and
`geom_track_bar()` shows intervals relative to a baseline.

### Inspect retention {#tracks-diagnostics}
Use `export_ggchord_layout()` to inspect `track_registry` and `track_diagnostics`.
Their original value limits, physical mm contributions and native offsets have
different units. Focus tracks with `focus_ggchord_track()` alongside the same loci;
check clipped or omitted rows rather than treating an absent bar as zero.

### Combine bars, a line and categorical tiles {#tracks-multiple}

```{r example-27, eval=FALSE}
line_bins <- transform(bins, pos = floor((start + end) / 2), signal = signal / 2)
categories <- data.frame(accver = "A", start = c(100, 500, 800),
  end = c(250, 700, 950), category = c("one", "two", "one"))
p_multitrack <- ggchord(seqs[1, ]) + geom_seq() +
  geom_track_bar(aes(track_value = signal, track_fill = signal), data = bins,
    position = position_track("signal", width = unit(5, "mm"))) +
  geom_track_line(aes(track_value = signal), data = line_bins,
    position = position_track("signal", width = unit(5, "mm")), colour = "#244B68") +
  scale_track_value_continuous("signal", limits = c(-1, 1), unit = "arbitrary units") +
  scale_track_fill_gradientn("signal", colours = c("#31537D", "#F3F4EE", "#D26B38")) +
  geom_track_tile(aes(track_fill = category), data = categories,
    position = position_track("sites", side = "outside", order = 2, width = unit(2, "mm"))) +
  scale_track_fill_manual("sites", values = c(one = "#6E9E88", two = "#DCBA66")) +
  coord_circular()
focused_bins <- focus_ggchord_track(bins, seqs[1, ],
  loci = data.frame(accver = "A", start = 100, end = 700), type = "interval")
```

![Shared-domain bar and line with an independent categorical track](../man/figures/multitrack.png)

The bar and line deliberately share `signal` and one domain; the line is half the
bar's synthetic signal, not another measured sample. Both declare the same width.
The categorical `sites` lane has an independent ID and fill scale. Baseline zero
participates in domain training. Explicit limits must represent the intended
measurement domain; changing a value scale does not move the track in space.
`focused_bins` retains interval clipping/source mapping for the selected locus.
Inspect track diagnostics for bounds clipping instead of treating omitted rows
as zero. See [styling](#styling-roles) for track colour versus fill roles.

The line uses integer bin midpoints rounded down. The second categorical band
is explicitly outside and ordered after the numeric band; narrow inside bands
may fold at small radii and are rejected rather than drawn through the centre.


## Primers, restriction and feature search {#recognition}

### Search and display are separate {#recognition-search}
A tiny synthetic sequence demonstrates exact primer and restriction searches:


```{r example-28, eval=FALSE}
target <- c(circle = "TTGCAAAAAGAATTCACG")
primers <- find_primer_bindings(target, primers = c(test = "ACGTTGCA"),
  min_annealed_bases = 8)
sites <- find_restriction_sites(target, enzymes = "EcoRI", methylation = "none")
p_sites <- ggchord(data.frame(accver = "circle", length = nchar(target))) +
  geom_seq() + geom_primer(data = primers) +
  geom_restriction_site(data = sites) + coord_circular()
```


The primer crosses the circular origin. Set `circular = FALSE` for a linear
sequence. Search hits are computational matches, not experimental validation.
Primer `"three_prime"` mode finds an exact suffix, with no mismatch model;
its Wallace melting-temperature estimate is a composition heuristic.

### Restriction interpretation {#recognition-restriction}
`find_restriction_sites()` returns unfiltered matches and cleavage coordinates;
`filter_restriction_sites()` selects a display set. Enzyme site counts refer to
the full supplied sequence and remain stable after filtering. `methylation =
"auto"` uses audited context only for exactly recognized bundled references;
it does not claim unknown samples are unblocked. This synthetic example explicitly
uses `"none"`. `geom_restriction_site(leader = "radial")` is the default route.

### General feature recognition {#recognition-features}
`find_common_features()` supports curated exact-reference annotations, DNA and
record-specific matching modes. Protein searches use standard-code six-frame
translation; they do not implement splicing, alternative initiation or
origin-crossing protein matches. Source genetic-code metadata does not select
another translation table. For nonstandard codes use DNA matching or external
code-aware analysis. Confidence is a heuristic label, not a probability.
Use [explicit CDS projection](#projection) for known protein/genome maps.

### Follow an annotated reference workflow {#recognition-reference}
The short synthetic sequence isolates search mechanics. The [complete pUC19
workflow](#plasmids) demonstrates catalogue annotations, exact reference
matching, site display filtering, primer labels and feature stacking together.
Changing only a sequence name does not make it a recognized reference; sequence
content determines source-backed recognition. Read the result methods and
methylation provenance instead of assigning reference claims to an unknown sample.


## Explicit homologs and coding-coordinate links {#homology}

### Membership is supplied evidence {#homology-membership}
After the [shared setup](#shared-setup), this declared synthetic cluster
connects one feature on each sequence. It is a teaching assertion, not an
inference from the repeated gene annotation text.


```{r example-29, eval=FALSE}
cluster_features <- transform(genes, feature_id = paste0("gene", 1:3))
membership <- data.frame(feature_id = cluster_features$feature_id, cluster_id = "demo_cluster")
homologs <- link_ggchord_clusters(cluster_features, membership,
  pairs = data.frame(qaccver = c("A", "B"), saccver = c("B", "C")))
loci <- find_ggchord_loci(seqs, cluster_features, targets = "gene1", upstream = 50, downstream = 100)
p_homologs <- ggchord(seqs) + geom_link_ribbon(data = homologs$data, fill = "#9CBBAF") +
  geom_seq() + geom_gene(data = genes) + geom_seq_label() + coord_collinear()
```

![Declared synthetic cluster links, not a computed alignment](../man/figures/homologs.png)

Inspect `homologs$report$comparisons` and `$members`. Unknown members are omitted
and reported; ambiguous paralogs default to omission. `paralogs = "all"` explicitly
requests bounded Cartesian products. Repeated feature IDs require an explicit
segment policy, and an outer span is an anchor, not an exon alignment.
`find_ggchord_loci()` selects exact feature IDs and expands in biological direction;
unknown direction requires symmetric extensions. Continue with [focus](#views).

### Project a declared protein correspondence {#homology-projection}

```{r example-30, eval=FALSE}
paired_coding <- data.frame(feature_id = c("a", "b"), accver = c("A", "B"),
  start = c(10, 100), end = c(18, 108), strand = c("+", "-"), phase = 0)
paired_cds <- build_ggchord_cds(paired_coding)
protein_link <- data.frame(qfeature_id = "a", sfeature_id = "b",
  qstart = 1, qend = 2, sstart = 2, send = 3)
projected_links <- project_ggchord_links(protein_link, paired_cds, ungapped = TRUE)
```

| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| `genomic_features` | 1 |
| `projected_links` | 1 |

Equal protein endpoint spans are not evidence of ungapped alignment. The explicit
`ungapped = TRUE` assertion is required. The helper splits where either CDS crosses
a coding-segment boundary and preserves source protein metadata. It does not emit
protein identity as nucleotide identity or invent nucleotide alignment length.
For domains and partial/phase policies, see [CDS projection](#projection).


## CDS coordinate projection {#projection}

### Build an explicit coding map {#projection-map}
This synthetic split codon spans two coding segments:


```{r example-31, eval=FALSE}
coding <- data.frame(feature_id = "cdsA", accver = "A", start = c(100, 200),
  end = c(103, 204), strand = "+", phase = c(0, 2))
cds <- build_ggchord_cds(coding, genetic_code = 11)
domains <- data.frame(feature_id = "domainA", parent_id = "cdsA", start = 2, end = 3)
genomic <- project_ggchord_features(domains, cds)
```


`genomic$segments` preserves the actual coding pieces, not an envelope including
introns. `project_ggchord_links()` similarly projects explicit protein links;
it does not compute new homology or translate DNA.

### Phase, partial ends and exceptions {#projection-phase}
CDS segments share `feature_id`, one sequence and a known strand. GFF3 `phase`
counts from each biological 5-prime end to the next codon boundary. Only the
first phase is skipped; later phases check accumulated coding length, retaining
codons split across segments. Explicit `segment_order` can declare an origin join.

Partial ends default to an error. `partial = "trim"` explicitly excludes bases
without complete codons; residue one means the first complete observed codon.
Genetic-code IDs are metadata for coordinate projection, not translation choices.
Declared frameshifts, slippage, translation exceptions and unsupported location
operators are rejected. No unobserved protein length or identity is inferred.

### Inverse mapping {#projection-inverse}
Use `project_ggchord_features(genomic, cds, from = "genome")` to map back.
Non-codon boundaries require an explicit `codon_boundary` policy. Source
coordinates, parents and projection provenance remain attached. Read the full
function reference (`help("project_ggchord_features", package = "ggchord")`) before applying
this to partial or multi-segment biological models.

### Project feature links as well as domains {#projection-links}
The domain example above maps an observed residue interval through explicit CDS
segments. [Coding-coordinate links](#homology-projection) adds a paired model
and demonstrates the separate ungapped assertion. Neither helper translates DNA,
validates genetic code or creates a new alignment. Compare the retained segment
pieces and source metadata before drawing discontinuous genomic anchors.


## Focus, segments and homology {#views}

### Focus without losing origins {#views-focus}
After the [shared setup](#shared-setup):


```{r example-32, eval=FALSE}
focused <- focus_ggchord_data(seqs, links, genes,
  loci = data.frame(accver = c("A", "B", "C"),
    start = c(50, 100, 300), end = c(600, 600, 950)))
p_focus <- ggchord(focused$seq_data, focused$ribbon_data, focused$gene_data) +
  geom_seq() + geom_link_ribbon() + geom_gene() + geom_seq_break() +
  scale_seq_position_continuous(coordinates = "source") + coord_collinear()
```

![Focused comparisons with source-coordinate axes](../man/figures/focus.png)

Focus relocates retained positions to local one-based coordinates and retains
source origins, truncation flags and a report. `boundary = "trim"` can clip
links by a linear display projection; it does not realign sequences. A scaled
alignment length is flagged as estimated. `coordinates = "source"` restores
source axis labels, including after repeated focusing.

### Independent windows and local reversal {#views-segments}

```{r example-33, eval=FALSE}
windows <- data.frame(accver = c("A", "A"), start = c(50, 650),
  end = c(400, 950), locus_id = c("A_left", "A_right"),
  row_id = "A", orientation = c(1, -1))
segmented <- segment_ggchord_data(seqs[1, ], windows = windows)
p_segments <- ggchord(segmented$seq_data) + geom_seq() +
  coord_collinear(segments = segmented$segments, segment_gap = 80)
```


Each window has a reversible source mapping; omitted gaps have no mapping.
`map_ggchord_position()` maps explicit source positions into a plot for ordinary
ggplot2 annotations. Supply the window ID when windows share a source sequence.
Do not interpret display orientation as a change to the original strand.

### Explicit biological relationships {#views-homology}
`find_ggchord_loci()` selects declared feature/name queries. `link_ggchord_clusters()`
requires an explicit membership table and sequence pairs; equal gene names do
not establish homology. `filter_ggchord_ribbons()`, `deduplicate_ggchord_ribbons()`
and `merge_ggchord_ribbons()` prepare existing alignments, preserving source
membership and estimated-length flags. Bundle and density statistics summarize
provided links rather than creating new sequence alignments.

### Map an annotation back to source coordinates {#views-mapping}

```{r example-34, eval=FALSE}
source_mark <- map_ggchord_position(p_focus, "A", 200, source = TRUE)
p_marked <- p_focus + ggplot2::geom_point(data = source_mark, aes(x, y),
  inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#A23B40", size = 2)
```


Run the [focus example](#views-focus) first. The helper returns Cartesian x/y
for source position 200 on A. It does not make all ordinary ggplot2 coordinates
become genomic bp. In segmented views choose the window ID, and check positions
in omitted gaps rather than extrapolating across them. Use [explicit homologs](#homology)
when the locus selection comes from declared feature/cluster evidence.


## Mappings, scales, guides and themes {#styling}

### Build styles from data roles {#styling-roles}
Run the [shared setup](#shared-setup). The example declares categories
explicitly: ribbon fill maps query ID; sequence colour maps sequence ID; gene fill
maps strand. Manual scale names match those values exactly.


```{r example-35, eval=FALSE}
p_styled <- ggchord(seqs, links, genes) + geom_seq() +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = qaccver), alpha = .3) + geom_gene() +
  geom_seq_label() + coord_collinear() +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = c(A = "#487A6A", B = "#B68048", C = "#637DA0")) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = c("+" = "#B68048", "-" = "#637DA0")) +
  scale_ribbon_fill_manual(values = c("A" = "#D4E5D8", "B" = "#E3D9C8", "C" = "#D4DFEB")) +
  guides(gene_fill = guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  theme_ggchord_publication() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
theme_variants <- list(minimal = theme_ggchord_minimal(), dark = theme_ggchord_dark(),
  plasmid = theme_ggchord_plasmid())
```

![Explicit manual scales and grouped legends](../man/figures/styling.png)

| Role | Mapped data | Useful scale family |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `seq_colour`, `seq_ring` | Sequence/category | Sequence colour or ring manual scales |
| `ribbon_fill`, `ribbon_alpha`, `ribbon_colour`, `ribbon_linetype` | Alignment metadata or statistics | Manual, gradient/steps/identity and alpha scales |
| `feature_fill`, `feature_shape`, `gene_fill`, `region_fill` | Annotation category or strand | Role-specific manual/preset scales |
| `link_colour`, `link_alpha`, `link_linewidth`, `link_linetype` | Point-link metadata | Continuous or manual link scales |
| `track_value`, `track_fill`, `track_colour` | Values/categories in one named track | Named value domain and colour/fill scales |

### Fixed styles and user scale priority {#styling-priority}
Put a constant style outside `aes()`. Map variable styles inside it and supply an
appropriate scale. An explicitly fixed geom value takes precedence; omitting that
argument keeps mapping active. Your scale takes priority over automatic defaults.
Repeated same-kind layers keep independent data/mapping/parameters. A geometric
vector named by `accver` does not mean a scale also accepts per-sequence lists.

### Make legends readable {#styling-guides}
`guide_ggchord_legend()` controls discrete role legends; `guide_ggchord_colourbar()`
controls continuous colour guides. The colour/color spelling aliases are retained,
with `colour` preferred in this documentation. Use `show.legend` on a layer,
`guides()` for guide choices and `theme(legend.position = ...)` for placement.
A wide guide may need multiple rows or a wider export, not smaller biological data.

### Select a theme for the scene {#styling-themes}
The example stores minimal, dark and plasmid alternatives in `theme_variants`.
Add the appropriate object to the matching plot. `theme_ggchord_publication()`
is used above; the plasmid preset belongs with the circular workflow. These
objects style non-data appearance. They do not choose a coordinate system or
replace data-driven fill scales. Use `theme(text = element_text(...))` for text
appearance; removed `base_size` constructor-style shortcuts have a
[migration route](#migration).


## Common adjustments and grammar {#adjustments}

### Assign each responsibility {#adjustments-grammar}
| Task | Interface |
| --- | --- |
| Map a column to an aesthetic | `aes()` |
| Define mapping and guide | `scale_*()`, `guides()` |
| Geometry and fixed style | `geom_*()` |
| Local placement | `position_*()` |
| Global coordinate system | `coord_*()` |
| Non-data appearance | `theme_*()`, `theme()` |
| Titles and captions | `labs()` |

Fixed styles may be supplied directly to geoms. Data-driven variation needs a
mapping and scale. An explicit fixed value overrides its mapping; omitting the
fixed argument preserves the mapping. User scales override inferred defaults.
`shape` is the fixed feature geometry parameter; `feature_shape` remains the
mapped role. Explicit `shape = NULL` is invalid, not a request to use a mapping.

### Map link identity {#adjustments-mapping}
After the [shared setup](#shared-setup):


```{r example-36, eval=FALSE}
p_mapped <- ggchord(seqs, links) + geom_seq() +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = pident)) +
  scale_ribbon_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#E7EFEA", "#246D68")) +
  coord_chord(rotation = 20) + labs(title = "Sequence comparison") +
  theme_ggchord() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


### Place features {#adjustments-position}
Use `position_strand(c("+" = .1, "-" = -.2))` for signed strand offsets.
`position_feature_stack()` handles overlapping features; `position_track()`
allocates a named quantitative lane. Geometric sequence parameters accept one
value, a matching unnamed vector, or a vector named by `accver`; named vectors
are recommended. This syntax does not extend to scales, guides or themes.

Each layer owns its own `data`, `mapping` and parameters. Repeated feature or
link layers do not replace one another. Use ordinary ggplot2 `show.legend` and
`inherit.aes`; role input mappings precede geometry, while staged visual mappings
follow ggplot2 evaluation. See the API contract (`help("ggchord_api_contract", package = "ggchord")`).


## Export, preview and diagnostics {#output}

### Save the intended size {#output-size}
After creating `p_collinear` in [three modes](#modes):


```{r example-37, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("comparison.png", p_collinear, width = 8, height = 5, units = "in", dpi = 144)
```


RStudio's Plots pane uses the current panel size and can rearrange labels and
guides. Preview at the same explicit dimensions before final `ggsave()`:


```{r example-38, eval=FALSE}
view_ggchord(p_collinear, width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")
diagnosis <- diagnose_ggchord(p_collinear, width = 8, height = 5, units = "in")
```


`view_ggchord()` returns a temporary image path; it does not keep a final export.
The website, README and vignettes share PNG assets exported through standard
`ggsave()` at sizes listed in the [gallery](#gallery). They do not capture an
interactively resized panel. Use your intended PDF/SVG device explicitly for
final vector output; font availability and embedding remain device-dependent.

### Consume geometry by name {#output-geometry}

```{r example-39, eval=FALSE}
geometry <- export_ggchord_layout(p_collinear, include = "seq")
rows <- unique(geometry$seq[c("layer_id", "component", "source_row")])
```


`export_ggchord_layout()` is the recommended layer-aware table interface.
`get_chord_layout()` retains the complete documented layout; neither is deprecated.
Select named fields, not fixed column positions. `source_row` indexes resolved
layer input; IDs are build-local resources, not permanent biological identifiers.
See the complete layout contract (`help("ggchord_layout_contract", package = "ggchord")`).

### Interpret evidence {#output-diagnostics}
`diagnose_ggchord()` separates measured panel size from geometry convergence.
A measured panel does not certify collision-free text, font embedding or all
applications. Inspect warnings, text/guide measurements and placement reasons.
`optimize_ggchord_layout()` applies documented opt-in adjustments; retain a copy
and inspect the result. Previews and diagnostics use independent render copies.
Direct mutation of shared ggproto layer environments retains ordinary ggplot2
reference semantics; it is not an automatically isolated edit.

### Complete layout, tables and opt-in ordering {#output-consumption}

```{r example-40, eval=FALSE}
full_layout <- get_chord_layout(p_collinear)
layer_tables <- export_ggchord_layout(p_collinear, include = c("seq", "gene"), original_data = TRUE)
layout_choice <- optimize_ggchord_layout(seqs, links, optimize = c("order", "orientation"), weight = "count")
```


Create `p_collinear` in [three modes](#modes-collinear) first.
`full_layout` retains the complete documented getter result. `layer_tables`
selects sequence/gene tables and resolved original data; it is not a raw-file
archive. Layer IDs and source-row roles distinguish independent same-kind layers.
Empty components can lack a fixed column prototype. Select fields by name.

`layout_choice` optimizes declared order/orientation using count weighting because
the synthetic links have no reported alignment-length column. It returns a choice
for explicit use in sequence settings; it does not mutate the plot or establish
biological orientation. Save the choice and compare the result before adopting it.
The export asset manifest (`website/assets/plots.csv` in the source repository) records exact documentation sizes.


## Frequently asked questions {#faq}

### Why are labels different after resizing? {#faq-resize}
The available physical space changed. Use [explicit-size preview and saving](#output-size).
Check hidden-label diagnostics; do not infer missing input rows from absent text.

### Why did an old parameter stop working? {#faq-removed}
The API cleanup removed execution of old aliases. Use the [migration table](#migration).
Do not mix old and new spellings for one semantic setting. The colour/color
function spelling aliases remain, with `colour` preferred in documentation.

### Why is a feature rejected as a gene? {#faq-strand}
The gene shortcut requires known `+`/`-` strand. Keep unknown strand in a general
feature layer; do not guess `+`. Amino-acid intervals require explicit projection.

### Why is a ribbon missing in linear mode? {#faq-ribbons}
By default ribbons connect adjacent displayed sequences. Inspect pair selection,
clipping and validation. Use explicit `pairs` or `adjacent_only = FALSE` deliberately.
This default does not remove original input records.

### Can the package compute alignments or validate primer experiments? {#faq-biology}
It visualizes supplied alignments and computational search results. It does not
run BLAST, infer clusters from names or validate wet-lab outcomes. Search confidence
is not a probability. See [recognition limitations](#recognition).

### Is a measured diagnostic a release certification? {#faq-quality}
No. It describes a requested render. Platform/device/font checks, full vignettes
and package checks belong to an explicitly authorized release. This development
version has only scoped documentation verification.

### Where should I report a problem? {#faq-report}
Use the [issue tracker](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/issues) with a small input,
package/ggplot2 versions, code, intended width/height, device and diagnostic output.
Avoid attaching private sequence data; a synthetic reproduction is usually enough.


## Migrate to the candidate API {#migration}

### Scope and timing {#migration-scope}
These are current candidate replacements, not a v1.0.0 compatibility promise.
Earlier 0.16.x versions are locally completed but unreleased. Old calls in this
table explain migration and must not be executed as current examples. Exact
first-removal tags are not guessed where historical evidence gives only an upper bound.

### Replacement table {#migration-table}
| Old (do not run) | Current | Removal / guard | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `geom_ribbon()` | `geom_link_ribbon()` | ≤ 0.16.1 | Renamed link layer; not ggplot2::geom_ribbon(). |
| `ggchord(..., rotation = 20)` | `ggchord(...) + coord_chord(rotation = 20)` | ≤ 0.16.1 | Global coordinates are composed with +. |
| `geom_feature(feature_shape = "block", feature_width = .05)` | `geom_feature(shape = "block", width = .05)` | 0.16.1 | Mapped feature_shape is retained. |
| `geom_gene(gene_offset = c("+" = .1, "-" = .2))` | `geom_gene(position = position_strand(c("+" = .1, "-" = -.2)))` | 0.16.1 | Explicit Position values are signed. |
| `geom_feature(feature_offset = .1)` | `geom_feature(position = position_strand(.1))` | 0.16.1 | Use a Position object. |
| `geom_gene(gene_width = .05)` | `geom_gene(width = .05)` | 0.16.1 | Fixed geometry uses the shared width name. |
| `geom_link_ribbon(ribbon_gap = .01)` | `geom_link_ribbon(link_gap = .01)` | 0.16.1 | Use link_gap; likewise use link_ctrl_point. |
| `geom_gene_label_repel(gene_label_layout = "aligned")` | `geom_gene_label_repel(label_layout = "auto")` | 0.16.1 | Migrate both the name and value. |
| `geom_gene_label_repel(label_rotation = 90)` | `geom_gene_label(label_rotation = 90)` | 0.16.4 guard | Previously ignored manual control now errors; alternatively remove it. |
| `geom_feature_label_repel(label_orientation = "horizontal")` | `geom_feature_label(label_orientation = "horizontal")` | 0.16.4 guard | Use the fixed feature-label layer for unknown-strand features. |
| `geom_restriction_site(leader = "trunk")` | `geom_restriction_site(leader = "radial")` | 0.16.1 | The radial default remains. |
| `theme_ggchord(base_size = 10)` | `theme_ggchord() + theme(text = element_text(size = 10))` | ≤ 0.16.1 | Text appearance belongs to theme elements. |

### Run the replacement {#migration-replacement}
After [setup](#shared-setup) and the `features` table in
[circular mode](#modes-circular):


```{r example-41, eval=FALSE}
p_migrated <- ggchord(seqs[1, ]) + geom_seq() +
  geom_feature(data = features, shape = "block", width = .05) +
  geom_feature_label(data = features, label_rotation = 0) + coord_circular()
p_offsets <- ggchord(seqs, gene_data = genes) + geom_seq() +
  geom_gene(position = position_strand(c("+" = .1, "-" = -.2)))
```


Old minus-strand offset magnitudes need a negative sign in explicit Position
values. Mapping still uses `aes(feature_shape = type)` with a shape scale;
the fixed parameter is `shape`. Automatic labels use `label_layout`; manual
geometry uses the corresponding fixed-label layer. `label_layout = "aligned"`
becomes `"auto"`. Removed names are errors, not silently retained execution paths.

### What remains supported {#migration-retained}
The five colour/color spelling aliases, all upstream reexports, gene/feature/plasmid
shortcuts and both geometry getter/export interfaces remain. Coordinate-specific
defaults and already documented result fields are retained. See the
API contract (`help("ggchord_api_contract", package = "ggchord")`) and current reference for
NULL/NA/missing semantics; NULL does not universally mean disabled.


## Reproducible gallery {#gallery}

### One source for both languages {#gallery-source}
Figures use repository-backed sequences/annotations or explicitly synthetic
teaching inputs, defined in the shared
[documentation example source](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/blob/main/tools/documentation-examples.R).
No raw FASTA/GFF3/BLAST record was changed to improve appearance. The same image
bytes are used by both languages, README and vignette; captions provide localized
interpretation. The source and asset hashes are recorded in the asset manifest (`website/assets/plots.csv` in the source repository).

Real-data and plasmid articles state each display filter; synthetic track
values, cluster membership and small input tables are not biological observations.

### Reproduce {#gallery-reproduce}
From the source repository, with its suggested development dependencies available:

```sh
Rscript tools/documentation-plots.R
python3 tools/sync-tutorials.py --check
python3 tools/build-website.py
python3 tools/check-documentation.py
```

The PNG device is used only to update these documentation figures. This is not
an output-device matrix or release validation. Source code and dimensions live
in `tools/documentation-plots.R`; changing the figure parameters requires
regenerating the manifest. See [output](#output) for your own export.

## Terminology and design sources {#glossary}

### Shared terminology {#glossary-terms}
| English | 现代汉语 | API / units |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sequence | 序列 | accver / length |
| chord diagram | 弦图 | coord_chord() |
| circular sequence map | 单序列圆图 | coord_circular() |
| collinearity plot | 共线性图 | coord_collinear() |
| interval link / ribbon | 区间连接 / 连接带 | qaccver / saccver |
| feature | 通用注释特征（feature） | geom_feature() |
| gene | 已知链的基因 | geom_gene() |
| strand | 链方向 | + / - / unknown |
| aesthetic mapping | 美学属性映射 | aes() |
| scale | 标度 | scale_*() |
| guide | 图例 / 标度指南 | guides() |
| position | 局部位置调整 | position_*() |
| track | 定量轨道 | position_track() |
| genomic position | 基因组位置 | one-based inclusive bp / 一基闭区间 |
| layout units | 原生布局单位 | not bp or mm / 不等于 bp 或 mm |
| source row | 已解析输入来源行 | source_row |
| physical file line | 物理文件行 | .source_line |
| focus | 局部聚焦 | focus_ggchord_data() |
| segment | 分段窗口 | segment_ggchord_data() |
| leader | 标签引导线 | label / connection |
| CDS projection | 编码序列坐标投影 | build_ggchord_cds() |
| measured panel | 已测量面板 | not visual certification / 不等于视觉认证 |

### Design and asset provenance {#glossary-sources}
The grammar follows [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/): mappings, scales,
geometry, positions, coordinates and themes retain distinct responsibilities.
Compact query/subject field names follow BLAST-style tables; ggchord does not run
an alignment tool during drawing. Circular hierarchy and feature readability
are compared with Circos, clinker and DNA Features Viewer, as recorded in the
repository design documents. These are conceptual comparisons, not copied APIs.

The detailed ggchord artwork was supplied by the user on 2026-11-01 for this
website and documentation. Full-size PNG and WebP preserve every decoded RGBA
pixel. Only the small navigation thumbnail is resized. See the image manifest (`website/assets/icon.json` in the source repository)
for source hashes and exact sizes. The compact hexagonal study mark below, site
CSS/JS and documentation diagrams are original project assets under the
repository MIT terms. The study mark is supplementary, not a replacement for
the supplied artwork.

![Compact hexagonal study mark](../man/figures/logo.svg) System fonts are used; no webfont, icon
library or third-party image is downloaded. Plot colours come from the package's
existing defaults or explicit teaching code; those literal colour choices are
listed with the source. The site uses the existing Pandoc and R documentation
converters at build time without bundling their binaries or stylesheets.
